title: Power Automate: export work queue items to CSV from the automation center
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout facts match the roadmap, and Microsoft Learn supports the Premium licensing requirement and Dataverse access controls. Independent searches confirmed the stated gaps about the native CSV export, including its administrator switch, columns and export-specific licensing.

claims.claim: Dataverse security roles control access to the automation center's underlying work queue data.

claims.claim: In standard Dataverse environments, necessary automation center privileges are included in the default environment maker role.
claims.quote: In standard Dataverse environments (production, trial, sandbox, and developer), necessary privileges are included in the default environment maker role.

claims.claim: In Default environments with a provisioned Dataverse database, all users automatically become environment makers.

claims.claim: Custom security roles can provide narrower access to automation center data.
claims.quote: Additionally, administrators can create custom security roles with row-level privileges to control the data users can view and interact with.

claims.claim: Assigning security roles requires at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table.

claims.claim: The System Administrator role has the required role-assignment privileges by default.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Dataverse RBAC for limiting work queue use in API-based scenarios.
claims.quote: if you want to limit the use of work queues in cloud flow and API-based scenarios, you should use Dataverse RBAC to control access to the underlying tables.

claims.claim: Work queues hold process-relevant data for processing by automations or people.
claims.quote: with the highest-priority items being completed first, regardless of whether they've been processed by digital workers, human workers, or through integrations.
